    13  
    14  /-!
    15  # Maschke's theorem
    16  
    17  We prove **Maschke's theorem** for finite groups,
    18  in the formulation that every submodule of a `k[G]` module has a complement,
    19  when `k` is a field with `Fintype.card G` invertible in `k`.
    20  
    21  We do the core computation in greater generality.
    22  For any commutative ring `k` in which `Fintype.card G` is invertible,
    23  and a `k[G]`-linear map `i : V → W` which admits a `k`-linear retraction `π`,
    24  we produce a `k[G]`-linear retraction by
    25  taking the average over `G` of the conjugates of `π`.
    26  
    27  ## Implementation Notes
    28  
    29  * These results assume `IsUnit (Fintype.card G : k)` which is equivalent to the more
    30    familiar `¬(ringChar k ∣ Fintype.card G)`.
    31  
    32  ## Future work
    33  It's not so far to give the usual statement, that every finite-dimensional representation
    34  of a finite group is semisimple (i.e. a direct sum of irreducibles).
    35  -/
    36  
    37  @[expose] public section
    38  
    39  noncomputable section
    40  
    41  open Module MonoidAlgebra
    42  open scoped Ring
    43  
    44  /-!
    45  We now do the key calculation in Maschke's theorem.
    46  
    47  Given `V → W`, an inclusion of `k[G]` modules,
    48  assume we have some retraction `π` (i.e. `∀ v, π (i v) = v`),
    49  just as a `k`-linear map.
    50  (When `k` is a field, this will be available cheaply, by choosing a basis.)
    51  
    52  We now construct a retraction of the inclusion as a `k[G]`-linear map,
    53  by the formula
    54  $$ \frac{1}{|G|} \sum_{g \in G} g⁻¹ • π(g • -). $$
    55  -/
    56  
    57  namespace LinearMap
    58  
    59  
    60  -- At first we work with any `[CommRing k]`, and add the assumption that
    61  -- `IsUnit (Fintype.card G : k)` when it is required.
    62  variable {k : Type*} [CommRing k] {G : Type*} [Group G]
    63  variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [Module k[G] V] [IsScalarTower k k[G] V]
    64  variable {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module k W] [Module k[G] W] [IsScalarTower k k[G] W]
    65  variable (π : W →ₗ[k] V)
    66  
    67  /-- We define the conjugate of `π` by `g`, as a `k`-linear map. -/
    68  def conjugate (g : G) : W →ₗ[k] V :=
    69    GroupSMul.linearMap k V g⁻¹ ∘ₗ π ∘ₗ GroupSMul.linearMap k W g
    70  
    71  theorem conjugate_apply (g : G) (v : W) :
    72      π.conjugate g v = MonoidAlgebra.single g⁻¹ (1 : k) • π (MonoidAlgebra.single g (1 : k) • v) :=
    73    rfl
    74  
    75  variable (i : V →ₗ[k[G]] W)
    76  
    77  section
    78  
    79  theorem conjugate_i (h : ∀ v : V, π (i v) = v) (g : G) (v : V) :
    80      (conjugate π g : W → V) (i v) = v := by
    81    rw [conjugate_apply, ← i.map_smul, h, ← mul_smul, single_mul_single, mul_one, inv_mul_cancel,
    82      ← one_def, one_smul]
    83  
    84  end
    85  
    86  variable (G) [Fintype G]
    87  
    88  /-- The sum of the conjugates of `π` by each element `g : G`, as a `k`-linear map.
    89  
    90  (We postpone dividing by the size of the group as long as possible.)
    91  -/
    92  def sumOfConjugates : W →ₗ[k] V :=
    93    ∑ g : G, π.conjugate g
    94  
    95  lemma sumOfConjugates_apply (v : W)
